summary: Texas Forest Service steel tower north of Clarksville, Red River County; built 1937; staffed by Juanita Westbrook from 1953; listed as standing, no access information found.

facts.design: steel lookout tower with a glass-enclosed watch room at the top; a 1954 report counts 126 steps to the top

staffing.status: crew leader in January 1966; no later staffing found in the sources read

events.note: Steel tower under construction in February 1937 north of Clarksville; concrete foundation excavated
W.J. Leatherwood named patrolman for the area; later named watchman, with Hugh Sheppard as relief man
Juanita Westbrook took over the tower in February 1953 as radio operator and fire spotter
Jerry Westbrook crew leader for the Negley crew area and its lookout tower in January 1966; last staffing found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A February 5, 1937 item gives 100 feet as the planned height; a February 17, 1937 item says the finished tower is 110 feet. We recorded 33.5 m (110 ft) as the finished height because that item describes the completed tower, but neither figure was checked against the structure.

notes_for_editor: Only the Forest Lookouts transcription page (newspaper clippings 1937-1966) and the FFLA Texas list were read. The 1937 and 1954 items are transcriptions; the original newspapers were not checked. The 1937 articles call the agency the Texas Forestry Service; the page header uses Texas Forest Service. A Facebook group post seen only in a search snippet, an aboutus.com page (elevation 137 ft, HTTP 429) and an NHLR entry (connection reset, guessed URL 404) were not read. Access level could not be determined, so facts.access is omitted. Check the NHLR/FFLOS for a register entry and current condition.
